thread:
elena: FYI we've got a high-priority report from Acme about intermittent 400s from the embeddings endpoint. They see "dimension mismatch" errors ~1-2% of requests during bursts. Customer is on Dedicated but using hosted embeddings route via our proxy.

sam: Can you paste the exact error and a minimal repro? Also which model header they send?

elena: Error from logs: `RuntimeError: embedding dimension mismatch: expected=1536 actual=768` (stack trace below). They say it only happens under load. Attaching snippets:

```
# server log
2026-03-10T22:41:12.234Z request_id=req_abc123 route=/v1/embeddings model=text-embed-redwood-xl
payload_size=12
ERROR embedding_batcher: computed_output_dim=768 expected_dim=1536 batch_id=42
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/runtime/serve/embeddings.py", line 214, in _flush_batch
    assert out.shape[1] == expected_dim
AssertionError: embedding dimension mismatch
```

elena: Customer request headers show `x-client-model: text-embedding-legacy` sometimes and `x-client-model: text-embed-redwood-xl` other times (they're doing gradual rollout).

sam: That smells like dynamic batching merged requests for two model variants with different vector sizes. If the batcher coalesces by route only (not model or dim) you'll get mixed-dim outputs and the assertion fails.

lina: Agreed. We had a related guard but it only keyed on route+tenant. If clients switch model headers mid-session, dynbatch will coalesce them.

raj: Is there any existing per-request model fingerprinting in the batching key? I thought we included model_version but maybe legacy header bypassed it.

sam: Current batch key: `tenant_id|route`. Proposed quick fix: append `model_id|embedding_dim` to the batch key so mixed-dim requests cannot be coalesced. Low-risk patch: compute dims from model metadata at enqueue time.

jordan: In the meantime, we can mitigate by asking the customer to set `max_batch_size=8` for their route and lower `batch_timeout_ms` to `10` to reduce coalescing window. That will reduce tail latency but also reduce throughput — need to warn them.

elena: Customer prefers a config change rather than asking devs to pin headers. They've already pushed half their traffic to the new model, so lowering max_batch_size is acceptable for now.

sam: Also log from the batcher shows tail latency spike correlates with large requests entering the queue and the coalescer waiting for small ones to fill the slot. Example timeline:

```
# p50/p95/p99 for route /v1/embeddings
2026-03-10T22:40:00 p50=12ms p95=40ms p99=600ms
2026-03-10T22:41:00 p50=14ms p95=48ms p99=1200ms (spike)
```

sam: If we reduce `max_batch_wait_ms` (aka `batch_timeout_ms`) we can cut p99 down. Alternatively enable `reject_mixed_models=true` to return 409 early for mixed dims so customer sees fast failure instead of 400 later.

elena: Can we craft a repro script for eng-runtime to reproduce locally? I wrote a small python script they can run:

```
# repro.py - send interleaved model headers at high QPS
import requests, time, threading
URL = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings'
H1 = {'Authorization': 'Bearer REDACT','X-Model':'text-embedding-legacy'}
H2 = {'Authorization': 'Bearer REDACT','X-Model':'text-embed-redwood-xl'}
PAY = {"input": ["test sentence"]}
def send(h):
    while True:
        try:
            r = requests.post(URL, json=PAY, headers=h, timeout=5)
            if r.status_code != 200:
                print(time.time(), r.status_code, r.text)
        except Exception as e:
            print('err', e)

# spawn mixed threads
for i in range(12):
    t = threading.Thread(target=send, args=(H1 if i%2==0 else H2,))
    t.daemon = True
    t.start()

time.sleep(30)
```

elena: Ran that locally against a dev instance and reproduced the assertion within 10s.

raj: OK. Plan: (1) short-term mitigation: ask customer to set max_batch_size=8 and batch_timeout_ms=10ms on their route (support can do this for Dedicated tenant). (2) medium-term: runtime change to include `model_id|embed_dim` in batch key + add a config flag `reject_mixed_dims` default false but opt-in via feature flag. (3) long-term: add telemetry to detect mixed-dimension enqueue attempts and surface alerts.

lina: I'll open a runtime PR for the batching key patch and add a unit test that simulates two model dims. I'll mark it for canary on dev-hosted first.

sam: Also let's add a temporary ACL on the coalescer to never mix legacy models until the rollout completes. We can map legacy header to its own queue.

eng-oncall-bot: @raj assigned to eng-runtime for 48h escalation. Incident ticket INC-2026-371 created.

support-bot: Updated customer slack with suggested config change and repro script. Customer replied :thumbsup: and asked for ETA on runtime fix.

raj: ETA for patch + canary is ~48 hours. Will post link to PR when created. For immediate relief I'll apply max_batch_size/batch_timeout override for Acme (requires ops assistance).

elena: Ops contacted, change scheduled in 15m. I'll follow up with the customer once applied. :white_check_mark:

jordan: Note — when we change batch key, test that we don't accidentally explode number of batch queues which would harm throughput; add adaptive memory cap.

sam: Agreed. Add tests for queue cardinality and perf benchmark at 10k qps.

elena: Closing loop: customer confirmed p99 dropped from ~1200ms to ~150ms after override. They still want the runtime fix but are unblocked.

raj: Filing follow-up: add telemetry alert when more than 0.1% of enqueues on a route attempt mixed-dim coalesce.

lina: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/4722 (WIP) — will update after tests.
